Redline round 2

Reviewed the fix diff from round 1 (1c96b8c..ff3f8d5), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at ff3f8d5.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at ff3f8d5 returned 6 candidates: 1 confirmed, 5 for the person, 0 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 0 already tracked, 0 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

The R1-1 fix puts the held-list rule in `redline-prefs.sh run drift`, where a prefs case pins it. The loop test shows that every prompt through the handoff comment replays on a record-commit resume, and that a freshly read list changes the comment first. The scripts header, `docs/scripts.md`, the skill, `docs/running.md` and README all describe it. The fix diff introduces no correctness bug. The one finding is a docs nit: the no-prompt relaunch in bypass-permissions is stated as fact, but the spec says it was never measured. The other candidates go to the person as gaps in hardening, scope or tests. This repository has no scheduled or queued work.

### Findings (0 correctness, 1 nit)

- **R2-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `docs/running.md:84` · Docs state the no-prompt relaunch in bypass-permissions as fact, though it was never measured

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

### For the person

- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:228` · R1-1 was decided, and its shape.md ("What it gives up") accepts one cost: an error resume before Finish (a failed `recheck r2`, say) keeps a stale agent list. In autopilot that list is `[]`, so the handoff comment names no agent file even when the resumed rounds ran in a reopened session that loads the edited agents. The shape says a narrower rule would need the workflow's label names. But an error marker already carries `stage`, so holding the list only for `kind == "error" and .stage == "finish"` (and for `stopped`) would need no label names.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:3134` · The Finish read trusts `round` whenever `error` is empty. On a run that posted, `last.round < finishing` cannot be true: it would mean the GitHub agent returned 0 for a failed read without setting `error`. Treating it as a failed read would harden the backstop for the PR #80 shape. That takes both a re-run round and an agent that ignores its prompt.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:223` · `run drift` reports only files under `agents/`. A self-review round can also edit `scripts/redline-gh.sh`, the other scripts, or README's "Git rules for Redline agents", and agents read all of these live. A reopened session also loads an edited `skills/redline/SKILL.md`. None of these is reported or pinned. Should the sentence cover them? That is a scope question for the author.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:230` · Pre-existing, not a regression. A run launched by the section 6 `scriptPath` fallback ran because the name is not registered in that session. While the workflow file is unchanged, `run drift` answers `name`, and a relaunch by name in the same session fails as not found. Section 7 has no fallback. The new routing could answer `scriptPath` with the live file in that case.
- `docs/running.md:122` · "Run markers and resume" still says a resume "relaunches with the marker's args plus `resume`". On the plugin's own repository a resume first runs `run drift`: it may go by `scriptPath` or be refused, and it adds `args.drift` with the held agent list (R1-1). Only "Hand-off and relaunch" says so. The #81 plan's first Docs entry said this section would name `run drift`, and the as-built entry moved that to "Saved launch settings".
- `tests/loop-test.mjs:1934` · No Finish-rule case covers a human review pass's summary. There is no human sequence with `lastPosted` above the nit-pass round that checks the summary comment and the record commit do not run. docs/running.md promises the same read for the summary.

**R2-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**Docs state the no-prompt relaunch in bypass-permissions as fact, though it was never measured**

docs/running.md:84 says that in bypass-permissions "the relaunch runs with no prompt". The skill's spoken line at skills/redline/SKILL.md:223 says "In bypass-permissions, which is how the plugin reviews itself, there is no prompt". The #81 spec's Unmeasured section (agent-os/specs/2026-11-12-1852-81-pin-relaunch-script-finish-rule/shape.md:81) and the PR description both say that "none in bypass-permissions" was not measured: only the headless denial was. Round 1's Decision 4 also says it is "still unmeasured". README Known limits (line 104, reworded in this fix diff) lists only the outside-bypass prompt count as unmeasured. So the person running a self-review is told as fact that no prompt will appear, and the README's list of what was not measured leaves this case out.

Proposed fix: Mark the bypass case as unmeasured in all three places. In docs/running.md "Hand-off and relaunch" (line 84) and in the skill's line at SKILL.md:223, write "in bypass-permissions it is expected to run with no prompt (not measured yet)". In README "Known limits" (line 104), change the second unmeasured item to "whether a relaunch from the pinned script asks exactly once outside bypass-permissions, and not at all in bypass-permissions".
